newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER DESPITE LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER DESPITE LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market rates, feeding on inflationary fears, edged higher on Friday even as liquidity returned, money market analysts said.
At the daily treasury bill auction, the tender rate put on 66 basis points to 23 percent with the central bank, uncomfortably aware of its rediscount rate at 23.5 percent, rejecting higher bids.
"We do not know whether we have reached the top yet as the outlook is clouded by inflation," one analyst told Reuters.

After opening with a shortage of $120.5 million and with treasury bill maturities worth $490 million, the Reserve bank offered the market $500 million. It was forced to reject the $300 million priced above 23 percent and took just $200 million.

In the secondary market treasury bills firmed to trade between 21 and 22.5 percent while call money and NCDs were volatile, ranging between 20 and 23 percent as traders sought to keep short positions in the rising market.
Analysts say the Reserve bank could be forced to revise its rediscount rate upwards if annual inflation, as expected turns out higher than the 19.9 percent recorded in the year to March.
